analysis: Examined .github/workflows/release-provider.yml. The patch adds a workflow-level env DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN: release (head lines 112-114) and bumps a validation-lane assertion from build_sdk_version '27.0' to '27.2' (head ~1444). The visible base units cover the surrounding signing/notarization flow, which is unchanged: Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, entitlement checks (get-task-allow absent, aps-environment production, keychain-access-groups), notarization and stapling, final-bytes smoke checks, CodeDirectory hash computation, and linked-SDK check against BUILD_SDK_VERSION, with the signing keychain deleted before running the app's CLI. The new env var is a non-secret toolchain selector consumed by scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and related scripts, which are not in the supplied evidence. It cannot be verified here whether that script enforces Xcode 27.2 and whether PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION (compared at the 'Fetch and verify' step, line 450) is updated consistently to 27.2; a mismatch would fail closed (the test at line 450 and the linked-SDK check), not open. No new secret exposure, no trust-boundary change, and no weakening of the attestation or code-identity binding (T-034, T-054, TB-009) is visible. The assertion bump is in a validation-only, unpublished lane. Remaining integration question: confirm that the scripts (prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh, provider-release-build action) honor DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release and pin the exact Xcode version/SDK, so that qualification and signing use the same toolchain. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a regression.
